fields.population: Alaska Native residents of Unalakleet (63 interviewed; 96.8% Alaska Native) and the population of US counties (households lacking complete in-home plumbing)
fields.sample_size: Chapter 3: 63 residents interviewed about seven water sources; Chapter 4: 3,143 counties, more than 12,000 county-year observations (American Community Survey and County Health Rankings, 2018-2021)
fields.effect_measure: three components: descriptive CBPR case study (Ch.2); fuzzy-set QCA of conditions producing trust or distrust in seven water sources (Ch.3); longitudinal county regression and spatial mapping of incomplete plumbing against physical and mental health outcomes (Ch.4)
fields.effect_estimate: Ch.3: trust in tap and bottled water depends on positive taste/odour/colour and perceived treatment; trust in wells, snowmelt and rainwater rests on Traditional Ecological Knowledge and social influence; organoleptics a core condition for every source. Ch.4 (as summarised in the dissertation abstract; the results chapter itself was not returned by the reader): plumbing poverty clusters in Alaska, Texas, Appalachia and the rural South, and counties with higher incomplete-plumbing rates report worse physical and mental health, with controls for social vulnerability, income inequality and demographics. No coefficients extracted.
fields.adjusted_or_unadjusted: Ch.4 adjusted (controls named in abstract); coefficients not seen
fields.covariates: Ch.4: social vulnerability, income inequality, demographics
fields.model_type: multi-method: descriptive community-based participatory research case study; fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis; longitudinal county-level regression with spatial mapping
fields.study_design: multi-method doctoral dissertation (three separate studies: CBPR case study, fsQCA interview study, county panel regression); not an integrated mixed-methods design
fields.risk_of_bias_rating: MMAT (re-appraised 2026-10-04 on the full text, partly read; supersedes the abstract-only rating of 2026-09-28). S1=Yes (each chapter states a research question); S2=Can't tell (Chapter 4 methods and results were not returned by the reader). Mixed-methods criteria: 5.1(rationale)=Can't tell (three chapters each use one method; no rationale for combining them as one design); 5.2(integration)=No (components are reported in separate chapters; only the introduction and conclusions link them); 5.3(meta-inference)=Can't tell; 5.4(divergence)=Can't tell; 5.5(component quality)=Can't tell (Chapter 3 fsQCA and Chapter 2 case study are described; Chapter 4 regression not read). Per MMAT's own guide, no composite score is computed.
fields.exact_location: Abstract pp xi-xv; Chapter 2 CBPR case study; Chapter 3 fsQCA methods pp 60-67 (Tables 1-5)
fields.table: Tables 1-5 (fsQCA elements, interview questions, conditions, calibration)

evidence_level: Single-study evidence: a three-part doctoral dissertation (Alaska Native CBPR case study; fsQCA of trust in seven water sources, n = 63; US county regression of incomplete plumbing on health, 3,143 counties) read in full text 2026-10-04 (partly: the Drive reader stopped inside Chapter 3). Its legal or administrative content is thin (tribal approvals for research; infrastructure inequity); the national regression result is taken from the abstract only.
pdf_note: PhD dissertation, Iowa State University, 2025; about 167,600 characters read (front matter, abstract, introduction, Chapter 2, start of Chapter 3 methods); Chapter 3 results and all of Chapter 4 were not returned by the reader
notes: ELIGIBILITY/SCOPE: three-part dissertation with thin legal content; country reset to United States (parenthetical text had been counted as multi-country). National regression result from the abstract only (reader stopped in Chapter 3).
